en.nativeSettings.aboutText:
Parlons is private, secure chat with nobody in the middle. Your messages go straight from your device to theirs, end to end, through whichever independent hosts are carrying traffic — no account, no phone number, no server holding your history. Your keys and your wallet never leave this phone.

Powered by Maxima · Minima
en.security.keyUseWarning: The wallet key-use count does not travel with your words. If this seed's key #1000 has ever signed on another wallet or node, don't send funds until you reconcile — reusing a one-time signing key can expose it and lose money. (A full encrypted backup preserves the real count; a words-only restore cannot.)

en.help.statusBody:
Maxima is a messaging layer, not a chat app talking to a server. This device may have no fixed address on the internet, so it borrows one: it connects OUT to a host, and that host passes anything addressed to you back down the same connection.

CONNECTED means at least one host is holding that connection open for you. NOT CONNECTED means nobody can reach you right now — you can still write messages, and they will be sent when a host comes back.
en.help.addressBody:
Two parts, joined by @.

Mx… is your identity. It is derived from your seed phrase and it never changes. It is also your public key, so anything sent to it can only be opened by you.

host:port is whichever host is currently relaying for you. That part DOES change — when a host goes away you get a new one. Your contacts are told automatically, which is what the Location Service is for.
en.help.hostsBody:
A host is any Maxima node with a port open to the internet. It relays traffic for devices that cannot accept incoming connections.

You attach to several at once (multi-homing). Classic Maxima picks exactly one, so when that one operator goes down you vanish. With three, two can fail and you are still reachable.

A host can read WHO you are talking to — the routing key is in the clear — but never WHAT: the message body is sealed end to end.
en.help.mlsBody:
A directory that answers one question: "what is the current address for this identity?"

Because your host part changes, a contact who has not heard from you in a while may hold a stale address. Rather than lose you, they ask an MLS.

"from host" means you are using whichever directory your host offers. PINNED means you chose one and will keep using it even if you change hosts.
en.help.contactsBody:
Someone whose identity key you hold and who holds yours. Adding a contact is a handshake, not a lookup: you introduce yourself to their address, and they reply with theirs.

Until they reply the link is one-way and you may not be able to reach them.
en.help.mailboxBody:
How many encrypted messages this device is holding on behalf of OTHER people who were offline when a message arrived for them.

It is ciphertext addressed to their key — this device cannot read a word of it. When they reappear, it is handed over and deleted.

Classic Maxima simply drops a message for an offline peer. This is the fix, and it works because many devices can each hold a little.
en.help.outboxBody: Your own messages that have not been accepted by a host yet. They are retried with a widening gap between attempts. A non-zero outbox that never falls means no host is reachable.
en.help.servicesBody:
Requests this device can answer for other people: directory lookups, mailbox pickup, address gossip, witness receipts.

A device with no public address can still answer them because a reply is sent as a NEW outgoing message rather than as a response on the incoming connection. Dialling out always works. That single change is what lets a client be a provider and not just a consumer.
en.help.contributionBody:
Maxima only works if enough participants carry traffic. Clients outnumber servers by orders of magnitude, so the network is far stronger if they help.

Everything here is opt-out and capped.
en.help.witnessBody:
Directory: you cache and serve identity → address lookups, so the directory is not a handful of servers everyone depends on.

Witness: you countersign "I saw message X at time T". It costs nothing and gives the network evidence of delivery that classic Maxima has no way to express.
en.help.storageBody: Holding small encrypted blobs addressed to a routing key, replicated across several devices so no single one has to stay online. Each blob is capped well under the 256 KB message ceiling.
en.help.directBody:
Normally this device borrows an address from a host. When conditions allow, it can instead get a REAL public address and receive messages directly — one hop shorter, and one fewer relay that sees who you talk to.

It only works when your router will hand out a public port (many will not). The device maps a port, then asks a host to dial it back from the outside — because a device testing its own port is meaningless. Only once that succeeds is the address advertised, so a dead address is never published.

"unavailable" is the normal result behind a NAT that won't forward. Nothing is wrong — you stay reachable through hosts as always. If your router needs a manual rule, add one under 'Port forwarding'.
en.help.countersBody:
mail held  – encrypted messages you are storing for offline peers
lookups     – directory questions you have answered
blobs         – stored blobs you are replicating
receipts    – witness signatures you have issued
addresses – address updates you have passed on to mutual contacts, so a peer who changed host is not orphaned
en.help.ticksBody:
⋯  queued — not handed to a host yet
✓  sent — a host accepted the bytes. This is ALL classic Maxima can ever tell you.
✓✓ delivered — the recipient's own device replied to say it has the message. In a group, every current member has.
✓✓ in blue — read.
✗  failed — no host would take it. It stays in the outbox.
en.help.readreceiptsBody:
Off by default. Delivery (two grey ticks) is always reported — that is the transport doing its job. Telling someone you have READ their message is information about you, so it is your choice.

Turning it on applies to everyone; there is no per-contact setting.
en.help.groupsBody:
A group message is sealed separately to every member and sent to each of them. There is NO shared group key.

That costs one send per member, and buys two things: removing someone removes them immediately (there is no key they still hold), and breaking one member's keys does not open the group.

Only an admin can change the roster, and only current members can post — checked on arrival, not just in the UI.
en.help.nameBody: What your contacts see instead of your key. Changing it sends an update to everyone you have — they hold the old one until then.
en.help.appearanceBody: Light, dark, or follow the system. "System" tracks your desktop's light/dark setting automatically; Light and Dark force one regardless. It is a look, nothing about it leaves this device.
en.help.seedBody:
24 words that ARE your identity. Your Maxima key is derived from them, so restoring the phrase anywhere reproduces exactly the same address and the same contacts can still reach you.

It is also a Minima WALLET seed. Anyone who reads it can spend any funds held against it. Write it down offline; never photograph it.
en.help.relaysBody:
host:port of any public Maxima node — a classic Minima node with Maxima enabled works too, this is fully interoperable.

More hosts means more independent routes to you. Adding or removing one restarts the transport.
en.help.logBody: Everything the transport did, newest first. This is a peer-to-peer network with no support desk: when something does not work, this is what tells you why.
en.help.keyusesBody:
Your wallet uses one-time Winternitz signatures. Each key has a limited number of available signatures.

The counter shows uses already reserved, and the caption shows how many remain. Signing reserves one use even if the payment does not complete. When all uses are consumed, this key cannot sign again.
en.help.nodekindBody:
Tell your contacts what this device is.

phone — an ordinary handset. core — an always-on Minima Core / full node running maxima. It only changes the label others see; it does not change how the transport works.

Android will kill a background connection to save power, which for a messaging transport means silently missing messages. Maxima asks to be exempt and holds the connection with a foreground service and an exact alarm.

If you deny the exemption the app still works, but expect gaps - particularly overnight.
en.help.ipcBody:
Other apps on this phone can use Maxima as their comms layer instead of shipping their own. They ask for permission, you approve them here, and each one owns its own message type so they cannot read each other's traffic.

Minima Core does not use this yet - it has no Maxima layer of its own, which is the gap this app exists to fill.

en.ios.pairIntro: Your identity, chats and contacts live on your always-on Parlons account. This phone pairs with it - nothing of the account is stored here but a device key. Scan the account's QR, or an invite QR that carries the pairing code too.
en.ios.codeHelp: Filled in by an invite QR. Otherwise: pair-code.txt on your server, Settings → Devices → New pairing code on a paired phone, or leave it empty and approve this phone from a paired one.
en.ios.accountFirst: New here? You need an account first
en.ios.ownAccountHelp: Parlons Cloud is a small program that keeps your account online: a machine that stays on, outbound internet only, no port forwarding, one command. A Raspberry Pi, a home computer or a small VPS all work. It prints a QR; scan it above.
en.ios.hostedHelp: Someone who runs a Parlons host can make an account for you and hand you an invite QR; scan it above and you are in. While it runs there, the host holds that account's keys, so choose a host you trust. You can move out at any time: an encrypted backup of the account restores on your own machine with the same address, and this phone keeps working without re-pairing.
en.ios.accountModel: One identity, one live account. The relays only ever carry sealed messages; the account is the only place that can open them.

en.nodeIde.about:
Your Parlons Node’s tooling, on your phone:

• Terminal — the full node command line with history, autocomplete and colorized output
• Scripts — KISS VM editor with lint, offline testing (the node’s own VM) and deploy
• Transactions — guided manual-UTXO transaction workbench
• Logs — the node’s rolling event log

Every command runs on the account’s node over the paired, end-to-end encrypted channel; output comes back complete, never cut. Long-press any output block to copy or share it.

en.scriptEditor.deployBody:
newscript registers this script's address with your node so it tracks coins locked by it. This does not spend anything.

NOTE: everyone who deploys the same script text gets the SAME address — with trackall on, your wallet shows every coin anyone ever locks there (this is how test/burn debris ends up in wallets). Leave trackall off for shared or template scripts.
en.scriptEditor.resultsHint: Check = parse + address · Run = execute in the node VM with your test inputs
en.scriptEditor.trackAll: trackall — track EVERY coin at this address, from EVERYONE. Identical script text means an identical address for all users: with this on, a standard template or a burn script fills your wallet with strangers’ locked coins. Leave off unless this script is uniquely yours.
en.scriptEditor.lintVariable: Variable '{name}' contains an underscore — underscored names silently fail on-chain. Use flat names (e.g. '{suggestion}').
en.scriptEditor.lintSize: Script is {length} chars — over the ~{limit} char limit scripts are silently rejected on-chain. Minify variable names or use MAST.
en.scriptEditor.lintNearSize: Script is {length} chars — approaching the ~{limit} char on-chain limit.
en.scriptEditor.lintBlockNum: @BLKNUM is unreliable on synced nodes — store a timeout in state and use @COINAGE instead.
en.scriptEditor.lintNumber: NUMBER(SHA...) overflows on a 32-byte hash — truncate first: NUMBER(SUBSET(0 4 SHA3(...))).
en.scriptEditor.lintReturn: No RETURN statement — a script must RETURN TRUE to be spendable.
en.scriptEditor.unsafeJson: {field} values can't contain spaces or ';' (they'd break the node command line). Use hex/number values.
en.scriptEditor.referenceBody:
KISS VM QUICK REFERENCE
(full docs: https://docs.minima.global)

VARIABLES
  LET myvar = 5
  LET hpk = PREVSTATE(0)
  NO underscores in names — they silently fail on-chain!

CONTROL FLOW
  IF cond THEN ... ELSEIF cond THEN ... ELSE ... ENDIF
  WHILE cond DO ... ENDWHILE
  ASSERT expression        (fails script if false)
  RETURN TRUE|FALSE        (must return a boolean)

STATE
  STATE(port)              read from the SPENDING transaction
  PREVSTATE(port)          read from the INPUT COIN (set at creation)
  SAMESTATE(start end)     assert STATE==PREVSTATE over a port range

SIGNATURES
  SIGNEDBY(pubkey)         tx signed by this key
  MULTISIG(n pk1 pk2 ...)  n-of-m signature check

TXN VERIFICATION
  VERIFYOUT(idx address amount tokenid keepstate)
    keepstate TRUE  = phase transition (output keeps state, storestate:true)
    keepstate FALSE = final payout (output must NOT store state)
  VERIFYIN(idx address amount tokenid)
  GETOUTADDR/GETOUTAMT/GETOUTTOK/GETOUTKEEPSTATE(idx)
  GETINADDR/GETINAMT/GETINTOK/GETINID(idx)
  SUMINPUTS(tokenid)  SUMOUTPUTS(tokenid)

CRYPTO
  SHA3(data)  SHA2(data)          32-byte hash
  CONCAT(a b)                     0xAA+0xBB -> 0xAABB
  SUBSET(start len data)          slice hex bytes
  NUMBER(hex)                     small hex -> number (max ~4 bytes!)
  Random pattern: LET r = NUMBER(SUBSET(0 4 SHA3(CONCAT(s1 s2)))) % range

GLOBALS
  @COINAGE   blocks since coin created  — USE THIS for timeouts
  @BLKNUM    current block — BROKEN on synced nodes, avoid
  @INPUT @AMOUNT @ADDRESS @TOKENID @COINID
  @TOTIN @TOTOUT @SCRIPT @FLOATING @CREATED @BLOCK

OPERATORS
  Compare:  EQ NEQ GT GTE LT LTE
  Boolean:  AND OR XOR NAND NOR NXOR NOT   (TRUE/FALSE only, NOT bitwise)
  Math:     + - * / %   (MiniNumber arbitrary precision)

HARD LIMITS (proven on-chain)
  ~1200 chars max script size — silently fails beyond
  1024 instructions per execution · 64 stack depth · 256 state ports
  NUMBER() on a full 32-byte hash overflows — SUBSET(0 4 ...) first

PROVEN RULES
  - Phase transitions: VERIFYOUT(... TRUE) + output storestate:true
  - Final payouts:     VERIFYOUT(... FALSE) + output storestate:false
  - Store timeout in state, check @COINAGE GT timeout
  - Set every state port your script reads — unset ports can crash
  - Test offline with Run (runscript) before deploying real funds

en.txnWorkbench.help:
The workbench builds raw UTXO transactions with the node’s txn* commands.

Rules it enforces for you:
• inputs must equal outputs — the difference BURNS
• sign BEFORE basics, then post
• status:true = accepted (async mining — istransaction:false is normal)
• delete abandoned txns or their input coins stay locked
en.txnWorkbench.storestate: storestate (keep txn state in this coin — covenants only)

en.commandHelp.helpPage:
help

Show help. With no parameters, list every command with a one-line summary.

In a summary [] marks a required parameter and () an optional one.

Chain multiple commands with ;

command: (optional)
    The command to show the full help page for.

Examples:

help

help command:send

status;balance
en.commandHelp.getaddressPage:
getaddress

Returns an existing default Minima address to receive funds, use as a change address etc.

Each address can be used securely 262144 (64^3) times.

Then you can wipe the private keys from your online node using the 'vault' command.

Examples:

getaddress

en.commandHelp.balancePage:
balance

Show your total balance of Minima and tokens.

address: (optional)
    Show the balance for a specific 0x or Mx address.

tokenid: (optional)
    Show the balance for a specific tokenid. Minima is 0x00.

tokendetails: (optional)
    true or false, show the complete details for the tokens

    Set the number of block confirmations required before a coin is considered confirmed in your balance. Default is 3.

    true or flase - show a much simpler view.. just the name and confirmed amount.

en.commandHelp.statusPage:
status

Show the general status for Minima and your node. Optionally clean the RAM.

Prints details for general status, memory used, chain info, stored txpow units, network connections, p2p connections and traffic.

clean: (optional)
    true only, clear the RAM.

debug: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Add debug detail: memory and per-file disk usage,
    chain tree and cascade internals.

complete: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Add the complete detail set: PoW mode (normal or low),
    block weights and the size of every database file.

Examples:

status

status clean:true
en.commandHelp.txnoutputPage:
txnoutput

Create a transaction output.

This will create a new coin (UTxO).

If the sum of inputs > outputs, the difference will be burned unless change to the sender is defined as an output.

Optionally store the transaction state variables in the new output coin.

id:
    The id of the transaction to add an output to.

amount:
    The amount for the output. To send to the specified address.

address:
    Address of the recipient/script to send the output to. Can be 0x or Mx address.

tokenid: (optional)
    tokenid of the output. Default is Minima (0x00).

storestate: (optional)
    true or false, true will keep the state variables of the transaction in the newly created output coin.
    Default is true.

Examples:

txnoutput id:simpletxn amount:10 address:0xFED5..

txnoutput id:multisig amount:10 address:0xFED5.. tokenid:0xCEF5.. storestate:false

txnoutput id:eltootxn amount:10 address:0xFED5..

en.commandHelp.txnaddamountPage:
txnaddamount

Add a certain amount to a transaction.

Use in conjunction with txncoinlock to create multiple offline transactions.

Output amount to an address OR only the change - if you have already added an output

id:
    The transaction id.

amount:
    The amount to add - in token units when tokenid is set.

address: (optional)
    The address to send the amount to. Not needed with onlychange:true.

onlychange: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Only add the inputs and the change output - you have
    already added the destination output yourself.

tokenid: (optional)
    The token to add. Default 0x00 (Minima).

fromaddress: (optional)
    Only select input coins from this address.

burn: (optional)
    The amount of Minima to burn with this transaction.

storestate: (optional)
    true or false, default true. Keep the state variables on the output coins.

split: (optional)
    Split the amount sent to address into this many output coins. Default 1.

Examples:

txnaddamount id:mytxn amount:10 address:Mx..

txnaddamount id:mytxn amount:10 onlychange:true

txnaddamount id:mytxn amount:10 address:Mx.. tokenid:0x.. split:4
en.commandHelp.txnautoPage:
txnauto

Create a complete transaction automatically: adds inputs for the amount, an output to
address, the change back to you and the MMR proofs, then optionally signs it.

Post it with txnpost.

id:
    The id for the new transaction.

amount:
    The amount to send.

address:
    The address to send to.

tokenid: (optional)
    The token to send. Default 0x00 (Minima).

sign: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Sign the transaction once it is built.

burn: (optional)
    The amount of Minima to burn with this transaction.

mmrscript: (optional)
    true or false, default true. Add the MMR proofs and scripts for the inputs.

Examples:

txnauto id:mytxn amount:10 address:Mx..

txnauto id:mytxn amount:10 address:Mx.. tokenid:0x.. sign:true

en.commandHelp.txnexportPage:
txnexport

Export a transaction as HEX or to a file.

The output can then be imported using 'txnimport' to another node. E.g. For signing.

id:
    The id of the transaction to export.

file: (optional)
    File name/path to export the transaction to, must use the .txn extension.

showtxn: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Include the transaction JSON in the response as
    well as the export data.

Examples:

txnexport id:multisig file:multisig.txn

Optionally specify an ID to use for the new transaction.

id: (optional)
    Choose an ID for the transaction you are importing.

file: (optional)
    File name/path to the previously exported .txn file.

data: (optional)
    HEX data of the previously exported transaction.

Examples:

txnimport data:0x0000..

txnimport id:simpletxn data:0x0000..

txnimport id:multisig file:multisig.txn
en.commandHelp.txninputPage:
txninput

Add a coin as an input to a transaction.

Optionally specify address, amount and tokenid to use an unspecified coinid - a floating ELTOO coin.

A floating coin can be attached to multiple different existing coins as long as it has the same

address, amount and tokenid - but different coinid.

id:
    The id of the transaction to add an input to.

coinid: (optional)
    The id of the coin to add as an input.

coindata: (optional)
    The data of the coin to add, instead of coinid.
    Can be from the 'coinexport' command or 'outputcoindata' from another transaction.

floating: (optional)
    true or false, true will add an unspecified, floating ELTOO coin as an input.
    If true, also specify address, amount, tokenid.
    If false, specify a coinid or coindata.

address: (optional)
    Coin address to use for the floating input. Can be 0x or Mx address.
    The coin that is used 
amount: (optional)
    Amount of a coin for the floating input.

tokenid: (optional)
    tokenid of a coin for the floating input.

scriptmmr: (optional)
    true or false, true will add the scripts and MMR proof for the coin.

Examples:

txninput id:simpletxn coinid:0xD0BF..

txninput id:multisig coinid:0xD0BF.. scriptmmr:true

txninput id:posttxn coindata:0x000..

txninput id:eltootxn floating:true address:0xFED5.. amount:10 tokenid:0x00
en.commandHelp.txnlistPage:
txnlist

Returns the full details of transactions.

    witness and the other row details.

Examples:

en.commandHelp.txnlockPage:
txnlock

When creating multiple transactions asynchronously you can ensure each is created one at a time.

action:
    lock - Gain a lock
    unlock - Release lock
    list/blank - Are we locked

timeout:
    How long to wait for the lock

unlockdelay:
    Wait this amount of milli after unlock.

Examples:

txnlock

txnlock action:lock timeout:10000

txnlock action:unlock unlockdelay:5000
en.commandHelp.txnminePage:
txnmine

Mine a transaction without posting it, from a stored transaction (id:) or from exported
transaction data (data:).

Post the mined result later with txnminepost.

id: (optional)
    The id of a stored transaction to mine.

data: (optional)
    Exported transaction data (from txnexport) to mine instead of a stored id.

Examples:

txnmine id:mytxn

txnmine data:0x..
en.commandHelp.txnminepostPage:
txnminepost

Post a transaction that was pre-mined with txnmine.

data:
    The pre-mined transaction data returned by txnmine.

Examples:

txnminepost data:0x..
en.commandHelp.txnmmrPage:
txnmmr

Add the MMR proofs to every input of a transaction that does not already have one.

id:
    The transaction id.

Examples:

txnmmr id:mytxn
en.commandHelp.txnpostPage:
txnpost

Post a transaction. Automatically set the Scripts and MMR proofs.

Optionally set a burn for the transaction.

id:
    The id of the transaction.

auto: (optional)
    Set the scripts and MMR proofs for the transaction.

burn: (optional)
    Amount in Minima to burn with the transaction.

mine: (optional)
    true or false - should you mine the transaction immediately.

txndelete: (optional)
    true or false - delete this txn after posting.

Examples:

txnpost id:simpletxn

txnpost id:simpletxn auto:true burn:0.1

txnpost id:multisig burn:0.1
en.commandHelp.txnscriptPage:
txnscript

Add scripts to a transaction.

id:
    The id of the transaction.

auto:
    Automatically add scripts you know. Useful for multi user transactions.

scripts:
    JSON holds the script and the proof in the format {script:proof}
    If it is a single script, and not one created with mmrcreate, leave the proof blank.
    If it is an mmrcreate script, include the proof.

Examples:

txnscript id:txnmast scripts:{"RETURN TRUE":""}

txnscript id:txnmast scripts:{"RETURN TRUE":"0x000.."}
en.commandHelp.txnsignPage:
txnsign

Sign a transaction.

Specify the public key or use 'auto' if the coin inputs are simple.

id:
    The id of the transaction to sign.

publickey:
    The public key specified in a custom script, or 'auto' for transactions with simple inputs.
    custom : sign with the privatekey: and keyuses: you supply.

txnpostauto: (optional)
    Do you want to post this transaction. Use the same values as you would for txnpost auto(sort MMR and Scripts)

txnpostburn: (optional)
    If you also post this transaction, do you want to add a burn transaction.

txnpostmine: (optional)
    If you also post this transaction, do you want to mine it immediately.

txndelete: (optional)
    true or false - delete this txn after signing AND posting.

password: (optional)
    If your wallet is password locked, unlock it for this signing and relock it afterwards.

privatekey: (optional)
    Use with publickey:custom. The 0x private key seed to sign with.

keyuses: (optional)
    Use with publickey:custom. How many times this private key has already signed. Every signature must use a
    fresh leaf of the key tree, so increase this by one for each signature you make.

Examples:

txnsign id:simpletxn publickey:auto

txnsign id:simpletxn publickey:auto password:your_password

txnsign id:multisig publickey:0xFD8B..

txnsign id:simpletxn publickey:auto txnpostauto:true

txnsign id:multisig publickey:custom privatekey:0x.. keyuses:5
en.commandHelp.txnstatePage:
txnstate

Add a state variable to a transaction.

id:
    The id of the transaction.

port:
    Port number of the state variable, from 0-255.

value:
    Value for the state variable.

Examples:

txnstate id:multisig port:0 value:0xFED5..

txnstate id:multisig port:1 value:100 

txnstate id:multisig port:1 value:"string"
en.commandHelp.txnviewPage:
txnview

View a transaction from previously exported HEX data or a .txn file.

file: (optional)
    File name/path to the previously exported .txn file.

data: (optional)
    HEX data of the previously exported transaction.

Examples:

txnview data:0x0000..

txnview file:multisig.txn
en.commandHelp.whitepaperPage:
whitepaper

Print the Minima white paper.

Examples:

whitepaper
en.commandHelp.tutorialPage:
tutorial

Show the complete grammar of the Minima KISS VM scripting language.

Examples:

tutorial
en.commandHelp.pingPage:
ping

Ping a host and get back Minima Node info.

host:
    The host:port of the Minima node to ping.

Examples:

ping host:
en.commandHelp.p2pstatePage:
p2pstate

Prints full details of the internal p2p state.

Includes details of your in and out connections and total peers.

Examples:

p2pstate
en.commandHelp.seedrandomPage:
seedrandom

Generate a random value, based on your SEED and a modifier.

modifier: 
    The modifier - added to seed before hash.

Examples:

seedrandom modifier:"Hello you"
en.commandHelp.testPage:
test

Developer command. Closes and reopens the node's SQL databases.

show: (optional)
    Accepted but unused.

action: (optional)
    Accepted but unused.

Examples:

test
en.commandHelp.tokenvalidatePage:
tokenvalidate

Validate the signature and webvalidate link in a token.

tokenid:
    The tokenid of the custom token/NFT to validate.

Examples:

tokenvalidate tokenid:0xFED5..
en.commandHelp.autominePage:
automine

Developer command. Currently a no-op in this node build: the enable: shown in older
summaries is disabled and is rejected as an invalid parameter.

Examples:

automine
en.commandHelp.mempoolPage:
mempool

Show the TxPoW in the mempool - the transactions and blocks the node holds that are not
yet in the cascade - with counts of transactions and blocks.

Examples:

mempool
en.commandHelp.randomPage:
random

Generate a random hash value, defaults to 32 bytes.

size: (optional)
    Integer number of bytes for the hash value.

type: (optional)
    sha3 (default) or sha2.

Examples:

random

random size:64
en.commandHelp.removescriptPage:
removescript

Remove a custom script. BE CAREFUL not to remove a script you need.

address:
    The address of the script.

Examples:

removescript address:0xFFE678768CDE..
removescript address:MxFFE678768CDE..
en.commandHelp.coincheckPage:
coincheck

Check a coin exists and is valid. Can only check unspent coins.

Returns the coin details and whether the MMR proof is valid.

data:
    The data of a coin. Can be found using the 'coinexport' command.

Examples:

coincheck data:0x00000..
en.commandHelp.timemilliPage:
timemilli

Return the current timemilli. Can go back minutes or hours.

minutesback: (optional)
    Go back this many minutes

hoursback: (optional)
    Go back this many hours

Examples:

timemilli

timemilli minutesback:120

timemilli hoursback:24
en.commandHelp.scriptsPage:
scripts

List all scripts or search for a script / basic address your node is tracking.

address: (optional)
    Script address or basic address to search for. Can be 0x or Mx address.

Examples:

scripts

scripts address:0xFED5..

scripts address:MxG087..n
en.commandHelp.quitPage:
quit

Shutdown Minima safely.

Ensure you have a backup before shutting down.

compact: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Compact the H2 databases while shutting down.
    Slower to quit but reclaims disk space.

Examples:

quit

quit compact:true
en.commandHelp.signPage:
sign

Sign the data with the publickey.

Returns the signature of the data, signed with the corresponding private key.

data:
    The 0x HEX data to sign.

publickey:
    The public key (0x..) of one of your wallet keys to sign with.

Examples:

sign data:0xCD34..
en.commandHelp.verifyPage:
verify

Verify a signature. Returns valid true or false.

data:
    The 0x HEX data to verify the signature for.

publickey:
    The public key of the signer.

signature:
    The signature of the data.

Examples:

verify data:0xCD34.. publickey:0xFED5 signature:0x4827..
en.commandHelp.checkaddressPage:
checkaddress

Check that an address is valid and show its 0x and Mx forms, and whether it is
one of your own wallet addresses.

address:
    The address to check, Mx.. or 0x.. A 0x address must be 66 characters long.

Examples:

checkaddress address:Mx..

checkaddress address:0x..
en.commandHelp.connectPage:
connect

Connect to a network Minima instance.

Connect to another node to join the main network or to create a private test network.

Set your own host using the -host parameter at start up.

host:
    The external ip:port of the node to connect to.

Examples:

connect host:94.0.239.117:9001
en.commandHelp.mathsPage:
maths

Run some maths with Minima MiniNUmber precision

Returns the result - na d full logs if required.

calculate:
    The maths you want calculated

logs: (boolean)
    true or false if you want the logs.

Examples:

maths calculate:"1+2 * (3/4)"

maths calculate:"1+2 * SIGDIG(1 3/4)" logs:true
en.commandHelp.scanchainPage:
scanchain

Scan back through the chain from the tip and list every transaction found.

depth: (optional)
    How many blocks to scan back. Default 16.

offset: (optional)
    How many blocks below the tip to start from. Default 0.

Examples:

scanchain

scanchain depth:100

scanchain depth:50 offset:100
en.commandHelp.disconnectPage:
disconnect

Disconnect from a connected or connecting host.

Optionally disconnect from all hosts.

uid:
    Use 'all' to disconnect from all hosts or enter the uid of the host to disconnect from.
    uid can be found from the 'network' command.

Examples:

disconnect uid:CVNPMLPOCQ0HQ

disconnect uid:all
en.commandHelp.slavenodePage:
slavenode

Connect to a master node and receive txblock messages.

host: (optional)
    Use with enable:true. The host:port of the master node to connect to.

enable: (optional)
    true or false. Turn slave node mode on or off. A restart is required.

Examples:

slavenode enable:true host:87.34.45.56:9001
en.commandHelp.decryptbackupPage:
decryptbackup 

Decrypt an encrypted backup.

file:
    Specify the filename or local path of the backup to restore

password: (optional)
    Enter the password of the backup 

output: (optional)
    Specify the output file 

Examples:

decryptbackup file:my-full-backup-01-Jan-22 password:Longsecurepassword456
en.commandHelp.messagePage:
message

Send a message to one or all of your direct peers.

data:
    The message as a string.

uid: (optional)
    Leave blank to send a message to all peers or enter the uid of the peer to send the message to.
    uid can be found from the 'network' command.

Examples:

message data:"hello" uid:CVNPMLPOCQ0HQ
en.commandHelp.convertPage:
convert

Convert between different data types

Returns converted data.

from:
    The type of the data param.

to:
    The type you want to convert to.

data:
    The the data to convert.

Examples:

convert from:String to:HEX data:hello

convert from:HEX to:Mx data:0XFFFF

convert from:String to:Base64 data:hello
en.commandHelp.hashtestPage:
hashtest

Check the speed of hashing of this device. Defaults to 1 million hashes.

Returns the time taken in milliseconds and speed in megahashes/second.

E.g. A speed of 0.5 MH/s indicates 500000 hashes per second.

amount: (optional)
    Number of hashes to execute.

Examples:

hashtest

hashtest amount:2000000
en.commandHelp.debugflagPage:
debugflag

Developer command. Set the node's DEBUG flag and an optional debug variable used by
test code.

activate: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Turn the DEBUG flag on or off.

var: (optional)
    Set the debug variable read by test code.

Examples:

debugflag activate:true

debugflag activate:true var:mytest
en.commandHelp.coinexportPage:
coinexport

Export a coin including its MMR proof.

A coin can then be imported and tracked on another node using the 'coinimport' command.

This does not allow the spending of a coin - just the knowledge of its existence.

coinid:
    The id of a coin. Can be found using the 'coins' command.

Examples:

coinexport coinid:0xCD34..

en.commandHelp.printmmrPage:
printmmr

Print the MMR set of the tip block and the total number of entries in the MMR.

Returns the tip block number, latest entrynumber and latest set of MMR entries.
For each entry, details of its row, entry number, data and value of all new and updated MMR entries for the tip block.

Row 1 represents the leaf nodes, entry 0 represents the first entry on a row.

Examples:

printmmr
en.commandHelp.healthcheckPage:
healthcheck

Return information about your chain, cascade and maxima.

Chain - tip:current chain tip block, root:current chain root block, chainlength:number of blocks in the heaviest chain.

Cascade - tip:current cascade tip block, tipcorrect:returns true if the cascade tip meets the root of the txpow tree.

Maxima - hosts:number of maxima hosts, contacts:number of maxima contacts.

Examples:

healthcheck
en.commandHelp.cointrackPage:
cointrack

Track or untrack a coin.

Track a coin to keep its MMR proof up-to-date and know when it becomes spent. Stop tracking to remove it from your relevant coins list.

enable:
    true or false, true will add the coin to your relevant coins, false will remove it from your relevant coins.

coinid:
    The id of a coin. Can be found using the 'coins' command.

Examples:

cointrack enable:true coinid:0xCD34..
en.commandHelp.sendviewPage:
sendview

View a transaction ( signed or unsigned ).

View the details of a txn created by the 'sendnosign' command by specifying its .txn file.

file:
    Name of the transaction (.txn) file to view, located in the node's base folder.
    If not in the base folder, specify the full file path.

Examples:

sendview file:unsignedtransaction-1674907380057.txn

sendview file:C:\Users\signedtransaction-1674907380057.txn
en.commandHelp.postfromPage:
postfrom

Post a transaction signed with signfrom.

data:
    The signed hex transaction data returned by signfrom.

mine: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Mine the transaction immediately.

mmr: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Recalculate the MMR proofs of the inputs before
    posting - use it if the transaction was created a while ago.

Examples:

postfrom data:0x..

postfrom data:0x.. mine:true mmr:true
en.commandHelp.mmrproofPage:
mmrproof

Check an MMR Proof.

Can be used to check MMR Proof of coins, scripts or a custom MMR tree created with the 'mmrcreate' command.

Returns true if the proof is valid or false if not.

data:
    String/HEX data of an MMR leaf node.

proof:
    The MMR proof of the data from the 'mmrcreate' command.

root:
    The root hash of the MMR tree from the 'mmrcreate' command.

Examples:

mmrproof data:0xCD34.. proof:0xFED5.. root:0xDAE6..
en.commandHelp.coinimportPage:
coinimport

Import a coin including its MMR proof.

Optionally you can track the coin to add it to your relevant coins list and know when it becomes spent.

Importing does not allow the spending of a coin - just the knowledge of its existence.

data:
    The data of a coin. Can be found using the 'coinexport' command.

track: (optional)
    true or false, true will create an MMR entry for the coin and add it to your relevant coins.

Examples:

coinimport data:0x00000..
en.commandHelp.tokensPage:
tokens

List all tokens in the unpruned chain.

Optionally import or export tokens to share token data.

tokenid: (optional)
    The tokenid of the token to search for or export.

action: (optional)
    import : Import token data from a previous export.
    export : Export the token specified by tokenid as data.

data: (optional)
    The data of the token to import, generated from the export.

Examples:

tokens

tokens tokenid:0xFED5..

tokens action:export tokenid:0xFED5..

tokens action:import data:0x000..
en.commandHelp.coinnotifyPage:
coinnotify

Listen for a specific coin address - without adding it to scripts.
You need to do this every startup.. from your Minidapp service.js for example

action: 
    add : Add to the list - only added once if already added.
    remove : Remove from the list
    check : Check if in the list.

address:
    The address to look out for.

Examples:

coinnotify action:add address:0xFFEEDD..

coinnotify action:remove address:0xFFEEDD..

coinnotify action:check address:Mx12ABGF56..
en.commandHelp.sendpostPage:
sendpost

Post a transaction previously created and signed using the 'sendnosign' and 'sendsign' commands.

Must be posted from an online node within approximately 24 hours of creating to ensure MMR proofs are valid.

file:
    Name of the signed transaction (.txn) file to post, located in the node's base folder.
    If not in the base folder, specify the full file path.

Examples:

sendpost file:signedtransaction-1674907380057.txn

sendpost file:C:\Users\signedtransaction-1674907380057.txn
en.commandHelp.systemcheckPage:
systemcheck

Developer command. Show the state of the node's internal message processors, or log
the full details of one of them.

processor: (optional)
    Use with action:details. One of main, txpowprocessor, txpowminer, p2pmanager,
    niomanager, notifymanager, senpollmanager, timerprocessor.

action: (optional)
    list : Show the message queue sizes of the main processors. The default.
    details : Log the full details of one processor. Use with processor:

Examples:

systemcheck

systemcheck action:details processor:p2pmanager
en.commandHelp.megammrPage:
megammr

View information about your MegaMMR. Export and Import complete MegaMMR data.

You must be running -megammr.

action: (optional)
    info   : Shows info about your MegaMMR.
    export : Export a MegaMMR data file.
    import : Import a MegaMMR data file.
    integrity : Check the integrity of a MegaMMR export file. Use with file:

file: (optional)
    Use with export and import.

Examples:

megammr

megammr action:export

megammr action:export file:thefile

megammr action:import file:thefile

megammr action:integrity file:megammr.dat
en.commandHelp.networkPage:
network

Show network status or reset traffic counter.

action: (optional)
    list : List the direct peers you are connected to. The default.
    reset : Restart the traffic counter from 0.
    recalculateip : Reset your IP - when you move to a different WiFi.
    restart : Restart the networking layer.
    loggingon : Turn on full network logging (NIO and P2P).
    loggingoff : Turn off full network logging.

Examples:

network

network action:list

network action:reset

network action:restart

network action:loggingon

network action:loggingoff
en.commandHelp.tracePage:
trace

Show the message stacks of the internal Minima Engine with optional filter string.

enable:
    true or false, true to enable or false to disable.

filter: (optional)
    A case sensitive string to filter the messages by.

network: (optional)
    true or false, show low level network messages

Examples:

trace enable:true

trace enable:true filter:MAIN

trace enable:true filter:MINER

trace enable:true filter:MDS

trace enable:true filter:MDS network:true

trace enable:true filter:NOTIFYMANAGER

trace enable:true filter:TXPOWPROCESSOR

trace enable:false
en.commandHelp.restorePage:
restore

Restore your node from a backup. You MUST wait until all your original keys are created before this is allowed.

file:
    Specify the filename or local path of the backup to restore

password: (optional)
    Enter the password of the backup 

shutdown: (optional)
    true or false, default true. Shut the node down once the restore completes, ready
    for a clean restart. false keeps it running.

Examples:

en.commandHelp.mmrcreatePage:
mmrcreate

Create an MMR Tree of data. Can be used in MAST contracts.

Must specify a JSON array of string/HEX data for the leaf nodes.

They could be a list of public keys.. and then in a script you can check if the given key is one in the set.

OR you can have different scripts.. and then you can execute any number of scripts from the same UTXO.

Returns the MMR data and proof for each leaf node and the MMR root hash.

nodes:
    JSON array of string/HEX data for the leaf nodes.

Examples:

mmrcreate nodes:["RETURN TRUE","RETURN FALSE"]

mmrcreate nodes:["0xFF..","0xEE.."]
en.commandHelp.hashPage:
hash

Hash the data or file - default SHA3.

Returns the hash of the data provided using the algorithm specified.

data:
    The data to hash. Can be HEX (0x) or a string in quotes.
    String data will return the the byte representation of the string.

file:
    The file path - can be the full path or relative to your base folder

type: (optional)
    sha2 or sha3. The hashing algorithm to use, default is SHA3.
    BTC and ETH support sha2 or sha3.

Examples:

hash data:0x1C8AFF950685C2ED4BC3174F3472287B56D9517B9C948127319A09A7A36DEAC8

hash file:myfile.txt

hash data:"this is my secret" type:sha2
en.commandHelp.printtreePage:
printtree

Default depth 32 blocks, can be increased to see more of the txpow tree.

depth: (optional)
    Number of blocks back from the tip to show in the txpow tree.

cascade: (optional)
    true or false, true shows the cascade.

Examples:

printtree

printtree depth:500

printtree cascade:true

en.commandHelp.backupPage:
backup

Backup your node. Uses a timestamped name by default.

password: (optional)

file: (optional)
    Specify a filename ending in .bak, optionally include a local path for the backup.

en.commandHelp.coinsPage:
coins

relevant: (optional)

    false will search all coins in the unpruned chain.

sendable: (optional)
    true only, filter out coins that are not sendable, they might be locked in a contract.
    Default is to return sendable and unsendable coins.

coinid: (optional)

amount: (optional)

address: (optional)
    Address of a coin to search for, could be a script address.
    Can be a 0x or Mx address.

tokenid: (optional)
    A tokenid, to search for coins of a specific token. Minima is 0x00.

checkmempool: (optional)
    Check if the coin is in the mempool.

coinage: (optional)
    How old does the coin have to be.

depth: (optional)
    How many blocks back to check from Blockchain tip.

order: (optional)
    Order asc or desc (Ascending or Decending).

megammr: (optional)
    Search the MegaMMR for coins too.

simplestate: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Return each coin's state as a simple
    {port:value} object instead of the full typed list.

totalamount: (optional)
    Return just enough of the matching coins to cover this amount, chosen with the
    same coin selection as send. In token units when tokenid is set.

state: (optional)
    Only return coins whose state variables contain this value.

Examples:

coins

coins relevant:true sendable:true

coins relevant:true amount:10

coins coinid:0xEECD7..

coins relevant:true tokenid:0xFED5..

coins relevant:true address:0xCEF6.. tokenid:0x00

coins relevant:true address:MxABC9..
en.commandHelp.consolidatePage:
consolidate

Consolidate multiple coins (UTxOs) into one by sending them back to yourself. Must have at least 3 coins.

Useful to prevent having many coins of tiny value and to manage the number of coins you are tracking.

Optionally set the minimum coin age (in blocks), maximum number of coins and maximum number of signatures for the transaction.

tokenid:
    The tokenid for Minima or custom token to consolidate coins for. Minima is 0x00.

coinage: (optional)
    The minimum number of blocks deep (confirmations) a coin needs to be. Default is 3.

maxcoins: (optional)
    The maximum number of coins to consolidate. Minimum 3, up to 20.
    Coins are first sorted by value (smallest first) before adding to the transaction.

maxsigs: (optional)
    The maximum number of signatures for the transaction, up to 5.
    Coins are then sorted by address to minimize the number of signatures required.

burn: (optional)
    Amount of Minima to burn with the transaction.

debug: (optional)
    true or false, true will print more detailed logs.

dryrun: (optional)
    true or false, true will simulate the consolidate transaction but not execute it.

password: (optional)
    If your Wallet is password locked you can unlock it for this one transaction - then relock it.
 
Examples:

consolidate tokenid:0x00

consolidate tokenid:0x77.. coinage:10

consolidate tokenid:0x00 maxcoins:5 password:your_password

consolidate tokenid:0x00 coinage:10 maxcoins:8 burn:1

consolidate tokenid:0x00 coinage:10 maxcoins:8 maxsigs:3 burn:1 dryrun:true
en.commandHelp.consolidatefromPage:
consolidatefrom

Consolidate the coins held at a specific address into one coin, signing with a private
key you supply.

fromaddress:
    The address whose coins are consolidated (Mx.. or 0x..).

script:
    The full KISS VM script of fromaddress, e.g. RETURN SIGNEDBY(0x..)

privatekey:
    The 0x private key seed that signs for fromaddress.

keyuses:
    How many times this private key has already signed. Every signature must use a
    fresh leaf of the key tree, so increase this by one for each signature you make.

tokenid: (optional)
    The token to consolidate. Default 0x00 (Minima).

mine: (optional)
    true or false, default true. Mine the transaction immediately.

burn: (optional)
    The amount of Minima to burn with this transaction.

maxcoins: (optional)
    Maximum number of coins to consolidate in one transaction. Default 50.

Examples:

consolidatefrom fromaddress:Mx.. script:"RETURN SIGNEDBY(0x..)" privatekey:0x.. keyuses:7

consolidatefrom fromaddress:Mx.. tokenid:0x.. script:"RETURN SIGNEDBY(0x..)" privatekey:0x.. keyuses:8 maxcoins:20

    true or false, true will clean the script to its minimal correct representation.

newscript trackall:false script:"RETURN (@BLOCK GTE PREVSTATE(1) OR @COINAGE GTE PREVSTATE(4)) AND VERIFYOUT(@INPUT PREVSTATE(2) @AMOUNT @TOKENID FALSE)"
en.commandHelp.peersPage:
peers

Prints the peers list this node has. P2P must be enabled.

Your peers are the other Minima nodes you know about.

action: (optional)
    list : List your peers. The default.
    addpeers : Add a list of new peers. 
    forcecheck : Force an immediate full check of all peers.
    publish : Write your top 20 peers to a file so they can be shared.
    fetch : Download a peers list from a URL and add those peers.

peerslist: (optional)
    CSV list of new peers [ip:port,ip:port,..]

max: (optional)
    Maximum number of peers to return with action:list or action:forcecheck.
    Default 1000.

file: (optional)
    Use with action:publish. The file to write the peers list to. Default peerslist.txt

url: (optional)
    Use with action:fetch. The URL to download a peers list from (as written by
    action:publish). The peers in it are then added.

Examples:

peers

peers action:list

peers action:addpeers peerslist:31.125.188.214:9001,94.0.239.117:9001

peers action:list max:10

peers action:forcecheck

peers action:publish file:peerslist.txt

peers action:fetch url:https://example.com/peerslist.txt

en.commandHelp.restoresyncPage:
restoresync

Restore your node from a backup and then sync to the top block using an archive node.

You MUST wait until all the keys for the node are created before this is allowed.

Reverts to a standard restore if backup is not older than 2 days.

file:
    Specify the filename or local path of the backup to restore

password: (optional)
    Enter the password of the backup 

host: (optional)
    ip:port of the archive node to sync from.

Examples:

restoresync file:my-full-backup-01-Jan-22 password:Longsecurepassword456 host:89.98.89.98:9001
en.commandHelp.rpcPage:
rpc

Enable and disable RPC on port 9005 (default is off).

Ensure your RPC port is secured behind a firewall before enabling.

The Deafult user is minima. That has write mode access. You can add other rpc users with read access.

enable:
    true or false, true to enable rpc or false to disable.

ssl:
    true or false, true to enable Self signed SSL - you can use stunnel yourself.

password:
    the Basic Auth password used in headers - ONLY secure if used with SSL.

username:
    the Username of an RPC user.

mode:
    the read or write mode of an RPC user.

action:
    adduser - add an RPC user.
    removeuser - remove an RPC user.
    listusers - list RPC users.

Examples:

rpc enable:true

rpc enable:true ssl:true password:minimarpcpassword

rpc enable:true password:minima

rpc action:adduser username:rpcuser password:rpcpassword mode:read

rpc action:removeuser username:rpcuser

rpc action:listusers

rpc enable:false
en.commandHelp.runscriptPage:
runscript

Test run a script with predefined parameters without executing on chain.

Scripts will be auto cleaned for you.

script:
    The script to run, surrounded by double quotes.

state: (optional)
    State variable values to use when running the script.
    JSON object in the format {0:value,1:value,..}.

prevstate: (optional)
    The previous state variable values (for the input coin) to use when running the script.
    JSON object in the format {0:value,1:value,..}.

globals: (optional)
    The Global variable values to use when running the script.
    JSON object in the format {@GLOBAL:value,..}.

signatures: (optional)
    The signatures required for the script. JSON array.

extrascripts: (optional)
    Extra scripts required for MAST contracts. 
    JSON object in the format {script:proof,..}.

Examples:

runscript script:"RETURN SIGNEDBY(0xFF..) AND @BLOCK GT 100" globals:{"@BLOCK":"101"} signatures:["0xFF"]

runscript script:"LET st=STATE(99) LET ps=PREVSTATE(99) IF st EQ ps AND @COINAGE GT 20
AND SIGNEDBY(0xFF) THEN RETURN TRUE ELSEIF st GT ps AND SIGNEDBY(0xEE) THEN RETURN TRUE ENDIF"
globals:{"@COINAGE":"23"} state:{"99":"0"} prevstate:{"99":"0"} signatures:["0xFF"]

runscript script:"MAST 0x0E3.." extrascripts:{"RETURN TRUE":"0x000.."}
